items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I said well Fred why not? Why don’t you bring your cello? I called rehearsal.

ctx.x: Let’s talk about why is it that you’re forming a group at this point that has this particular combination of instruments. I think that that’s something that historians would love for you to be able to express.

In all honesty that happened just by sheer accident. How I come about with the original quintet is that at first I wanted to get Gerry Wiggins, get a piano trio, but all the piano players that I liked, man, they had their own thing going so I decided to try something else. So I don’t know how I got in contact with Jim Hall. items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: Fred Katz was with me when I was with Lena. And I told Fred my plight. And we got to talking. So Fred said, “Well, Chic, if you like I’ll come over.”

ctx.x: That sound with the cello and pianoless. Did that come about from sitting down and thinking let’s find something different here? Or was it a more practical—

Originally the group was going to be French horn, John Graas, he was the number one French horn player on the West Coast at that time when I formed the group. The group was intact with Buddy and Jim Hall, and Carson. And Buddy and I came up musically together. Cars and I were with Gerry together, and Jim Hall was just a stroke of luck. He needed a gig and he heard that I was organizing, putting a group together. Because he was stacking music in a music store at that time. He wasn’t even playing. And the day of…
And even had the part where the stick fell.
